Compute marginal discovery rate and saturation curve

marginal_saturation_curve.Rd

Computes the instantaneous slope of the node and edge discovery curves (\(dN / dR\) and \(dE / dR\)) and the corresponding marginal (Good-Turing) saturation across a vector of downsampling fractions fracs.

Usage

marginal_saturation_curve(
  db,
  fracs = seq(0.04, 1, by = 0.04),
  components = NULL,
  min_degree = 1L,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

db

A PixelDB object with an active DuckDB connection.

fracs

A numeric vector of downsampling fractions in \((0, 1]\). Default is seq(0.04, 1.0, by = 0.04).

components

Optional character vector of component names to include. If NULL (default), all components are included.

min_degree

Integer (1L or 2L); minimum dynamic node degree at fraction p for a node to be counted. Default is 1L (all nodes). Set to 2L to track dynamic degree >= 2 core nodes.

verbose

Logical; if TRUE (default), print progress messages.

Value

A tibble with columns:

component

The component (cell) identifier.

read_count

Estimated number of reads at fraction p.

p

The downsampling fraction.

nodes

Expected number of unique nodes (with dynamic degree >= min_degree) at fraction p.

edges

Expected number of unique edges at fraction p.

degree

Estimated average node degree (\(2 \times \text{edges} / \text{nodes}\)).

node_discovery_rate

Instantaneous slope \(dN / dR\) at fraction p (new nodes per additional read).

edge_discovery_rate

Instantaneous slope \(dE / dR\) at fraction p (new edges per additional read).

degree_rate

Instantaneous slope \(d\bar{d} / dR\) at fraction p (change in average node degree per additional read).

marginal_node_saturation

Marginal node saturation at fraction p (\(1 - (dN / dR) / 2\)).

marginal_edge_saturation

Marginal (Good-Turing) edge saturation at fraction p.

Details

Marginal discovery rate across downsampling fractions

At any downsampling fraction \(p \in (0, 1]\), the expected number of retained edges is \(\mathbb{E}[E(p)] = \sum_{e=1}^{E} (1 - (1 - p)^{r_e})\). Differentiating with respect to the downsampled read count \(R(p) = p R\) gives the exact marginal edge discovery rate (new edges per additional read): $$\text{edge\_discovery\_rate}(p) = \frac{d\,\mathbb{E}[E(p)]}{dR(p)} = \frac{1}{R} \sum_{e=1}^{E} r_e (1 - p)^{r_e - 1}$$

For nodes:

  • When min_degree = 1L, \(\mathbb{E}[N(p)] = \sum_{v=1}^{N} (1 - (1 - p)^{r_v})\), so the exact marginal node discovery rate is: $$\text{node\_discovery\_rate}(p) = \frac{d\,\mathbb{E}[N(p)]}{dR(p)} = \frac{1}{R} \sum_{v=1}^{N} r_v (1 - p)^{r_v - 1}$$

  • When min_degree = 2L, a node has dynamic degree \(\ge 2\) at fraction \(p\) with exact probability: $$P(\text{deg}_v(p) \ge 2) = 1 + (d_v - 1)(1 - p)^{r_v} - \sum_{e \ni v} (1 - p)^{r_v - r_e}$$ Differentiating with respect to \(R(p) = p R\) yields the exact marginal discovery rate of dynamic degree \(\ge 2\) core nodes: $$\text{node\_discovery\_rate}(p) = \frac{1}{R} \sum_{v:\, d_v \ge 2} \left[ \sum_{e \ni v} (r_v - r_e)(1 - p)^{r_v - r_e - 1} - (d_v - 1) r_v (1 - p)^{r_v - 1} \right]$$

See also

marginal_saturation for computing full-depth marginal discovery rates and saturation as a lazy DuckDB table. approximate_saturation_curve for cumulative saturation curves.
